core.title: Make each plan decomposition unit's capability boundary legible from its description
core.given: Any decomposition unit of the plan (the bounded slice of the product the plan defines), whether newly added, changed, or existing and unchanged
core.when: the planner writes, updates, or reviews that unit's description
core.then: The description alone must make the unit's capability boundary (what it does and does not own) understandable later without the original conversation.
prefer: Write the description so a later reader can understand, from it alone, what the unit does and does not own.
Put the rationale in the plan schema's existing description field for the unit.
avoid: Introducing a new schema field (e.g. a separate rationale field) to carry the boundary or rationale.
Descriptions that only make sense with the planning conversation in hand (references to 'as discussed', unstated context).
core.why: Plan decomposition units outlive the conversation that created them, so a later reader must be able to tell from the description alone what the unit owns and does not own. Reusing the existing description field keeps the plan schema unchanged.
evidence: Each unit's description field, read in isolation, makes clear what the unit does and does not own.
No new field was added to the plan schema to hold rationale.
verification: Boundary-legibility half is reader-judged (llm_judged): verification reads each unit's description in isolation and judges whether what the unit does and does not own is clear; there is no mechanical oracle for this half.

No-new-field half: rationale must ride the plan schema's existing description field; detecting a rationale-like field newly added to the plan schema or to unit entries requires a schema/diff observer (needs_new_observer).

The rule declares no exceptions (its unless list is empty), so verification has no exception-based waiver path; per-rule severity and disposition, and this rule's verifier term ids, are realization details.

values: unit description does not convey what the unit does and does not own
rationale-like field added to the plan unit schema or unit entries

fires: The planner adds a new decomposition unit to the plan.
The planner edits a unit's scope or description.
The planner or a reviewer inspects an existing, unchanged unit whose description does not make clear what it does and does not own.
doesNotFire: Plan or doc content that does not define or describe any decomposition unit.
Code changes unrelated to plan decomposition definitions.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's local name for the plan's decomposition unit (the bounded slice of the product the plan defines) whose existing description field must carry its capability boundary and rationale; instantiating the core with this name reproduces the rule's concrete wording.

bunOnly.text: Term capability_boundary: what the wagon does and does not own, legible from its description alone.
bunOnly.reason: The term id 'capability_boundary' is this rule's verifier vocabulary in the ATDD-Bun realization; the neutral definition it names is carried by the core's then and verification (llm_judged half).

bunOnly.text: Term no_new_field: rationale rides the existing description field, not a new schema field.
bunOnly.reason: The term id 'no_new_field' is this rule's verifier vocabulary in the ATDD-Bun realization; the neutral definition it names is carried by the core's verification (no-new-field half).

neutralityNotes: The convention is essentially stack-neutral: it governs the content of plan artifacts, not code, and names no runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path. The only stack vocabulary is the local name of the plan's decomposition unit ('wagon' in ATDD-Bun), which the core refers to generically and which is supplied through the proposed profile key roles.plan_hierarchy#plan_artifact_unit_name. The verifier term ids (capability_boundary, no_new_field) have no neutral equivalent and remain bunOnly; the core's verification describes both halves generically, including that boundary legibility is llm_judged and that detecting a newly added rationale-like field needs a schema/diff observer. Activation fires/doesNotFire were neutralized the same way (unit name substitution) but are not separately numbered items.
